title: A Choir for the Wolf
premise: Odile Voss has survived the Thornfell mountains by knowing every road and trusting no one, so when a dying courier presses a blood-stained map into her hands, her instinct is to burn it. Instead she discovers the map is a living thing: drawn in the memory-ink of the vanished cartographer-guild, it shows the true face of King Aldric—revealing that the man on the throne is a hollow vessel animated by the usurper-mage Corvane, who devours royal memory to rule. Hunted by Corvane's inquisitors, Odile flees toward the free cities with the courier's brother, the disgraced royal chorister Emeric, whose songs can temporarily wake the king's buried self. As armies march and the map begins erasing Odile's own memories as payment for each secret it yields, she must choose between her survival and a love she barely has time to claim. In the throne room of the capital, Odile spends the last of her mapped memories to unbind Aldric from Corvane; the restored king destroys the usurper, but Odile remembers neither the war nor Emeric—until he sings the song he wrote for her, and something in her answers.
about_author: Ansel Eastwick is a former trail surveyor who spent six years mapping passes through the Carpathians before turning to fiction, a career he credits for his obsession with borders and the people who cross them. He writes in a cabin above the tree line, where he claims the silence is 'good for plotting treason.'

chapters.title: The Courier's Last Mile
chapters.summary: POV Odile. On a smuggler's road through Thornfell, Odile finds a courier dying of wounds no blade made, who presses a folded map into her hands and whispers a name before dissolving into ash. The map's ink moves. Odile, who has spent her life staying unmapped herself, feels her invisibility end. Emotional beat: dread disguised as irritation.

chapters.title: Ink That Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Odile. Studying the map in her safehouse, Odile learns it responds to touch, revealing hidden chambers and a royal seal—until an inquisitor's mark burns itself onto her wrist, marking her as claimed property of the crown. She flees as her safehouse burns. Emotional beat: the hunter realizing she has become the hunted.

chapters.title: The Singer in the Cellar
chapters.summary: POV Emeric. In the free city of Vell's Row, disgraced chorister Emeric recognizes the map's guild-mark and intercepts Odile, revealing the courier was his brother and that the songs he once sang for King Aldric were designed to hold the king's true self in place. He begs passage to the capital. Emotional beat: grief finding a purpose.

chapters.title: What the Map Costs
chapters.summary: POV Odile. Pursued through the mountain passes, Odile uses the map to find a hidden route—and watches it take a memory in payment: her mother's face. Emeric witnesses the transaction and understands what the journey will spend of her. Emotional beat: the first taste of the price, and the first real trust between them.

chapters.title: The Hollow King
chapters.summary: POV Emeric, in flashback and dream-song. Emeric's memories show the night Corvane took the throne: Aldric's memories devoured, his body puppeted, Emeric's choir silenced one singer at a time. Odile, reading the map's margins, realizes the guild didn't vanish—they were harvested. Emotional beat: the scale of the enemy revealed.

chapters.title: Free Cities, Chained Hands
chapters.summary: POV Odile. The free cities' council refuses to act without proof, and Corvane's armies close the passes. Odile offers the map as proof; the council demands it be surrendered, which would mean surrendering her memories with it. Emeric publicly sides with her, burning his last bridge to the old order. Emotional beat: love against duty, both directions.

chapters.title: The Song He Wrote for Her
chapters.summary: POV Emeric. Trapped in a burning waystation, Emeric sings to keep Odile anchored as the map devours whole years of her—her apprenticeship, her first map, the memory of why she chose invisibility. In the ash afterward, half-erased, she asks him why he stayed. He answers with the truth. Emotional beat: love confessed to someone who cannot remember it for long.

chapters.title: The Road Through the Usurper's Country
chapters.summary: POV Odile. With the passes sealed, the map offers one road: straight through Corvane's heartland, at a cost Odile refuses to calculate. They travel among refugees, and Odile, who once mapped realms for coin, begins mapping the faces of the displaced instead. Emotional beat: the cartographer learning that people are territories worth keeping.

chapters.title: Throne of Borrowed Years
chapters.summary: POV Emeric, then Odile. They infiltrate the capital during the king's memory-tithe ceremony. Emeric sings the waking-song as Corvane's inquisitors close in; Aldric's buried self stirs, and Corvane turns his full hunger on Odile and the map. She opens the map completely, offering everything it holds. Emotional beat: the climax—everything wagered at once.

chapters.title: A Choir for the Wolf
chapters.summary: POV Odile. Aldric wakes whole and unmakes Corvane with the accumulated memory of every stolen year; the map burns to blank vellum, taking Odile's memories of the journey with it. Weeks later, a free woman walks the rebuilt capital and stops, unaccountably, when a street singer begins a song she has never heard—and hums the harmony perfectly. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution—love outlasting memory.
